newsitem.title: USA: Winn-Dixie higher expenses, benefits hurt Q2.
newsitem.headline: Winn-Dixie higher expenses, benefits hurt Q2.

text.p: Winn-Dixie Stores Inc said on Wednesday an "unsatisfactory" sales increase and increased expenses, including benefit costs for part-time employees, affected the current quarter results.
The company's president, James Kufeldt, said he was disappointed with the results but encouraged by recent results.

"While disappointed with our results for the second quarter, we are encouraged by the sales and profit results for the last four weeks of the quarter, including an increase in identical store sales," he said.
Winn-Dixie said its second-quarter earnings were $47.7 million, or $0.32 per share compared to $72.5 million, or $0.48 per share.
Sales for the quarter increased to $4.06 billion from $3.97 billion.
